author: Primal Space
description:
By the 6th century, China had held a monopoly on silk production for over 3,000 years - but that was about to change.

During the reign of Justinian I, two monks were sent east on what was essentially an early industrial espionage mission. On their return, they reportedly smuggled silkworm eggs back to Europe hidden inside hollow walking canes.

Once the secret was revealed, the Byzantines were able to establish their own silk production, breaking China’s monopoly and turning silk into a major source of wealth and power for the empire.
title: The Silk Heist That Ended China’s Monopoly
